message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Atomic mass** | ~1.008 u (average over naturally occurring isotopes) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (¹H, 99.98 %), Deuterium (²H or D, 0.02 %) and Tritium (³H or T, radioactive, trace). |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14 K) – solidifies only at very low temperatures. |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) – boils at extremely low temperatures. |
| **Density** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C (gas); liquid density ~0.0708 g cm⁻³ at 20 K. |
| **Molar volume** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ at STP (standard temperature & pressure). |
| **Ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (first ionization energy). |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (negative, meaning it releases energy when gaining an electron). |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 (highest among all elements). |
| **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ (diatomic bond strength). |
| **Heat capacity (Cp)** | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 298 K (ideal gas value). |
| **Thermal conductivity** | ~0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 300 K (high for gases). |
| **Specific heat ratio (γ = Cp/Cv)** | 1.41 (ideal diatomic gas). |
| **Reactivity** | Extremely reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids, and many nonmetals. |
| **Flammability** | Highly flammable; reacts violently with oxygen to form water (combustion reaction). |
| **Oxidation states** | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride ion H⁻). |
| **Common compounds** | H₂O (water), H₂SO₄ (sulfuric acid), NH₃ (ammonia), CH₄ (methane), HF (hydrofluoric acid). |
| **Role in stars** | Fusion of two protons (hydrogen nuclei) into deuterium releases energy powering stars like the Sun. |
| **Applications** | Fuel cell technology (hydrogen fuel cells), rocket propellant (liquid hydrogen), industrial hydrogenation, semiconductor manufacturing, medical imaging (tritium as tracer). |

**Key Takeaways**

* Hydrogen is the lightest element, existing naturally as a diatomic gas (H₂) under normal conditions.
* It has a single proton and one electron, making it highly reactive and capable of forming both covalent and ionic bonds.
* Its isotopes have distinct nuclear properties: deuterium is stable and used in heavy water reactors; tritium is radioactive and used in nuclear fusion research and as a tracer in biochemical studies.
* Hydrogen’s high electronegativity and low ionization energy make it a powerful oxidizing agent and a key player in many chemical reactions, especially combustion and synthesis of organic molecules.
